description:
Marks a span of an episode and hands back the links that play it. Nothing is downloaded, transcoded or re-hosted: a clip is a pointer — the publisher's own URL plus an in and an out point — so the whole clip fits in its link and this call cannot fail for reasons of storage. The episode's name and cover are resolved and returned, so you can check you clipped what you meant to before sharing the link.

Times are seconds from the start of the episode, decimals allowed.

Returns `{ clip, links: { page, short, sourceAtMoment, mp3 }, shareText }`.

Usually followed by: share links.short (or links.page); links.mp3 downloads the audio.

audioUrl.description: The episode's audio file, when `url` is a page rather than the file. Pass the `audioUrl` from a resolve or an episode list: the clip then plays without waiting on the page to be read again.

end.description: Where it ends, in seconds. Must be at least half a second after `start`.

shorten.description: Also register the `/x/<id>` short link, which is the one thing this service stores. Set false to get only the self-contained long link and write nothing.

showUrl.description: The show this episode came out of (its feed). Pass the `showUrl` a resolve or an episode list gave you: it is what lets the clip page name the episode when its own page won't say, and what keeps a clip playable when the page moves.

start.description: Where the clip starts, in seconds from the start of the episode.

title.description: A title of your own for this clip, shown in place of the episode's on the clip's card, its page and the link's unfurl. The episode's name says which episode; this says what the clip is, which is what somebody scrolling past the link is deciding on. Trimmed to one line and cut at 50 characters, which is what the card holds without clamping on a phone. Leave it out and the episode's own name is used.
examples: The bit where he admits the model was guessing

url.description: The episode to clip. Use the `clipUrl` from list_episodes or resolve_url when you have one.

name: create_clip

Chapter.description: A moment the publisher named, from their own timestamp index.

startSeconds.description: Seconds from the start of the episode. Pass it to create_clip as `start`.

title.description: The publisher's own words for this stretch.

headline.description: The title passed as `title`, cleaned and capped — what the clip is called wherever it appears. Absent when none was given, in which case the episode's own title is used.

sourceUrl.description: Exactly what was passed in. Never rewritten — that's the promise.

title.description: The episode, as resolved. Check it before you share the link.

mp3.description: The clip as a file. Audio only, 10 minutes at most.

page.description: The clip, in a link that contains the whole clip.

sourceAtMoment.description: The publisher's own URL at that moment — no BitePods in the middle.

plays.description: Approximate: a per-clip counter, not an audit trail.

shortId.description: The id in `/x/<id>`, when one was registered.

audioUrl.description: The publisher's audio file, for an audio episode.

chapters.description: The publisher's own chapter marks, read from the episode notes. Absent when the show doesn't publish an index.

clipUrl.description: Pass this back as `url` to create_clip or get_transcript.

hasTranscript.description: Whether get_transcript will have anything to read.

pageUrl.description: The episode's own web page, when it has one of its own.

publishedAt.description: Unix seconds, when the source gave a date.

showUrl.description: The show this came out of. Pass it to create_clip alongside `url`.

total.description: Episodes the source listed, up to the 60-item cap.

code.description: The stable part. Branch on this, not on the wording.

Resolution.description: Read `type` first. All three are 200s: an unresolvable link is an answer, not a failure.

episodes.description: The first few; list_episodes returns the rest.

ResolvedEpisode.description: One playable episode. Nearly an `Episode`, but `sourceUrl` is the URL you passed in, unchanged — and a page that names nothing still resolves, so `title` can be absent.

clipUrl.description: Pass this back as `url` to create_clip or get_transcript.

Show.description: A show in the public podcast directory. Not playable on its own — resolve `sourceUrl` into episodes.

author.description: The publisher, as the directory names it.

feedUrl.description: The show's RSS feed, when the directory names one.

id.description: Stable within one answer; Apple's collection id when Apple answered.

rank.description: 1-based chart position, on chart answers only.

sourceUrl.description: What to pass to list_episodes: the feed, or the Apple page as a fallback.

country.description: Chart answers only: the country the chart is for.

Transcript.description: The publisher's own transcript, timed in seconds from the start of the episode.

estimated.description: True when long cues were split, so the split times are interpolated.

speaker.description: When the transcript says who's talking.

start.description: Seconds from the start of the episode — pass it to create_clip as-is.

reason.description: Why there are no lines, when `available` is false.

truncated.description: True when `limit` cut the answer; narrow the window or raise it.
